prompt: Write an email to a colleague about a new hobby you have taken up. Aim for about 400 words. Reply with the email only.
final_message:
Subject: Taking up bouldering (and why I'm now obsessed)

Hi Sam,

I hope your week is going well. I wanted to share something a bit outside my usual routine: a few months ago I took up indoor bouldering, and I've gotten far more hooked than I expected.

It started when a friend dragged me along to a climbing gym for a beginner session. I assumed it would be a one-off, something I'd try, enjoy mildly, and forget about. Instead, I spent two hours failing at a route that looked ridiculously easy from the ground, and I couldn't stop thinking about it afterward. I signed up for a membership the following week.

What I love most is that every climb is a puzzle. The routes are short, usually just a handful of moves, but figuring out where to put your hands and feet, how to shift your weight, and when to commit to a big reach takes real thought. After a day staring at spreadsheets, it's a wonderful change to use my brain and body together. I go in with a stressful head and come out feeling completely clear.

The community has been another pleasant surprise. Everyone at the gym is friendly and quick to offer advice. People who've never met will happily watch you struggle with a problem and then say, "Try turning your hip in on that second move." It's remarkably supportive for something that's technically individual. I've also noticed that failing is just part of the process. You fall onto a padded floor, laugh, and try again. I could stand to bring that attitude to my work.

Progress has been slow but satisfying. I started on the easiest grade, and I'm now working through the intermediate routes, though my forearms are not happy about it. I've learned the hard way that grip strength runs out well before enthusiasm does. Chalk, climbing shoes, and a lot of stretching have become part of my life.

I'm going two or three evenings a week, usually right after work, and I've been making a point of leaving my phone in the locker. It's become a nice boundary between the workday and the rest of my evening.

If you've ever been curious, I'd love to have you join me. The gym offers a free intro class, and there's no experience required. Even if you just want to watch and cheer me on while I flail at a problem for the tenth time, you'd be welcome. A few of us from the office could even make it a regular Thursday thing.

Let me know what you think, and I'd love to hear about any hobbies you've picked up lately too.

Best,
[name]
